regimens.dose_text: 10 mg/kg IV infused at a constant rate over at least 1 hour, every 8 hours for 10 to 14 days (up to 21 days in immunocompromised patients). Obese patients should be dosed using Ideal Body Weight (IBW). Maintain adequate patient hydration to prevent renal tubular crystal precipitation.

value.effect: Probenecid competitively inhibits renal tubular secretion of acyclovir, increasing acyclovir mean elimination half-life and AUC.
value.management: Monitor for acyclovir-induced neurotoxicity or nephrotoxicity when co-administering probenecid.

refs.quote: Coadministration of probenecid with acyclovir has been shown to increase the mean acyclovir half-life and the area under the concentration-time curve. Urinary excretion and renal clearance were correspondingly reduced.

value.effect: Coadministration of nephrotoxic drugs, pre-existing renal disease, and dehydration increase the risk of acute tubular necrosis and acyclovir crystallization.
value.management: Ensure adequate intravenous hydration and urine flow; monitor renal function frequently.

refs.quote: Concomitant use of other nephrotoxic drugs, pre-existing renal disease, and dehydration make further renal impairment with acyclovir more likely.

refs.quote: For patients who require dialysis, the mean plasma half-life of acyclovir during hemodialysis is approximately 5 hours. This results in a 60% decrease in plasma concentrations following a six-hour dialysis period. Therefore, the patient’s dosing schedule should be adjusted so that an additional dose is administered after each dialysis.
